dimensions.analysis: For the first several minutes the candidate repeatedly asked the interviewer to simply name the file, function, or line rather than working the failing assertion themselves, which is asking to be handed the answer rather than resolving genuine ambiguity. Only much later (370s-375s) did they ask a substantive clarifying question about whether shift windows are inclusive or half-open and whether the outgoing agent should be eligible at the handover minute, which is exactly the right ambiguity to resolve, but by then the interviewer had already had to push them there.

Before the second session restart, the candidate wandered through roster.py, router.py, and the ranking helper without ever stating a hypothesis about the mechanism, and even declared the ranking helper looked fine without explaining what check ruled it out. The actual mechanism (inclusive vs half-open shift boundary check) was only articulated at 405s, directly after the interviewer's explicit nudge at 380s handed them the half-open rule and told them to go check the on-shift code, so the strong mechanism statement was prompted rather than self-directed.

For roughly the first 300 seconds the candidate's narration was thin and mostly consisted of asking the interviewer to shortcut the search rather than explaining what each file read ruled in or out; the interviewer explicitly called this out at 266s. The one clear, well-narrated moment is the mechanism explanation at 405s, but it followed direct interviewer prompting rather than an unbroken account of their reasoning process.

The candidate stated the fix conceptually at 405s and was told to go make the change and run the suite at 595s, but the timeline shows no subsequent file edit before the session ended, and at 621s they were still asking the interviewer to confirm a line number rather than executing. There is no editing action visible to assess implementation quality against the stated plan.

The candidate ran the test suite twice early on but never ran it again after articulating the fix; instead of implementing and re-verifying, they asked the interviewer to confirm a colleague-supplied line number and then ended the session without making or checking any change.

At 405s the candidate gave a genuinely accurate account of the root cause — the inclusive offset<=span check disagreeing with the half-open Shift.covers, and the load-based rank key turning that overlap into the wrong winner — which matches the ground truth almost exactly. However this explanation came only after the interviewer supplied the half-open rule and handover expectation as a nudge, so it reflects understanding demonstrated under guidance rather than independently derived insight, and no verification followed to confirm the explanation held up in practice.
